_comment: Every call site of establishSession (auth/loginPaths.js scans them; auth/loginPaths.inventory.test.js holds this file to the scan) and what it does about a second factor. `mfa` is `enforced` (the second-factor step runs before this call for an account that has one), `not-applicable:<why>` (there is no second factor to ask for here), or `pending` (a known gap). `pendingAllowed` equals the number of pending entries and may only go down (zero since the OPAQUE path gained its second-factor step).

auth/login/finalizeLogin.js#password{....note: Same gate as above; the DEK is derived after the second factor and sealed at the store boundary (auth/sessionSeal.js).
Same gate as above; plan without encryption. The spread carries the sealed-session fields.

auth/login/finalizeLogin.js#password{pen.note: Same gate as above; the session is flagged pendingApproval for a waitlisted or unapproved account.

auth/login/finalizeOpaqueLogin.js#opaque.note: The OPAQUE proof parks the login in mfaPending when the account has a second factor; finalizeOpaqueLogin runs only after /auth/mfa/verify-login (or at once for an account without one).

auth/login/signupRoutes.js#signup{encryp.mfa: not-applicable:a new account has no second factor yet; enrolment happens after the first sign-in
auth/login/signupRoutes.js#signup{encryp.note: Self-signup or invitation, approved on the spot.

auth/login/signupRoutes.js#signup{pendin.mfa: not-applicable:a new account has no second factor yet; enrolment happens after the first sign-in
auth/login/signupRoutes.js#signup{pendin.note: Self-signup that waits for approval; the session is flagged pendingApproval.

auth/oauth/nextcloudLegacyRoutes.js#next.mfa: not-applicable:the Nextcloud instance authenticates the user over OAuth; its own second factor runs before it issues the token

auth/oauth/providerCallbackRoutes.js#oau.mfa: not-applicable:the identity provider authenticates the user (OAuth / OIDC); its second factor runs before the callback
auth/oauth/providerCallbackRoutes.js#oau.note: Microsoft, Google and the other configured providers; the audit method is the provider name.

auth/opaqueRoutes.js#opaque_register{opa.mfa: not-applicable:re-establishes the session of a user who already passed requireAuth to set the OPAQUE credential; not a sign-in
